subject: Mathematics
title: Vectors in Space
learningOutcomes: Recognise rectangular coordinates \((x,y,z)\) in space, the three coordinate planes and the eight octants.
Write a vector in terms of the unit vectors \(\hat i,\hat j,\hat k\) and identify its \(x,y,z\) components.
Find the vector \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) from the position vectors of its end points using Head \(-\) Tail.
Find the magnitude \(|\vec r|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}\) and the unit vector \(\hat r=\vec r/|\vec r|\).
Add, subtract and scale vectors in space, and use the distance and section formulae.
Prove the basic properties of vector addition: commutative, associative, zero vector and additive inverse.
Define the dot product, interpret it geometrically and find it from components.
Use the dot product for the angle between vectors, the condition of orthogonality and direction cosines.
Find the projection of one vector on another and the work done \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S\) by a constant force.
Define the cross product, state its direction by the right-hand rule and evaluate it as a determinant.
Use the cross product for the sine of the angle, a unit perpendicular vector, the parallel condition and moment of a force.
Find the area of a parallelogram and of a triangle using \(|\vec a\times\vec b|\).
Define the scalar triple product, write it as a determinant and prove its cyclic and swap properties.
Prove that dot and cross are interchangeable: \(\vec a\cdot\vec b\times\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b\cdot\vec c\).
Find the volume of a parallelepiped and of a tetrahedron.
Define coplanar vectors, apply the condition \(\vec a\cdot\vec b\times\vec c=0\), and apply vectors to real-world problems.

sections.heading: Scalars, Vectors and Position
sections.body: A scalar has magnitude only (mass, time, speed); a vector has magnitude and direction (force, velocity, displacement). A vector is drawn as an arrow from its tail to its head. The position vector of a point \(P(x,y,z)\) is \(\overrightarrow{OP}=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k\). For two points \(A\) and \(B\) use Head \(-\) Tail: \(\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec b-\vec a\).

sections.heading: Coordinates in Space
sections.body: Three mutually perpendicular axes \(Ox, Oy, Oz\) meet at the origin. They form three coordinate planes (\(xy\), \(yz\), \(zx\)) that divide space into eight octants decided by the signs of \(x,y,z\). A point with one zero coordinate lies in a coordinate plane; with two zero coordinates it lies on an axis.

sections.heading: Components, Magnitude and Unit Vectors
sections.body: Every vector in space is \(\vec r=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k\) where \(\hat i,\hat j,\hat k\) are unit vectors along the axes. Its magnitude is \(|\vec r|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}\). The unit vector in the direction of \(\vec r\) is \(\hat r=\vec r/|\vec r|\), and vectors are added, subtracted and scaled component by component.

sections.heading: Distance and Section Formulae
sections.body: The distance between \(P(x_1,y_1,z_1)\) and \(Q(x_2,y_2,z_2)\) is \(|\overrightarrow{PQ}|=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2+(z_2-z_1)^2}\). If \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) internally with \(AP:PB=m:n\), then \(\vec r=\dfrac{n\vec a+m\vec b}{m+n}\). The midpoint is \(\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{2}\) and the centroid of a triangle is \(\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}{3}\).

sections.heading: The Dot (Scalar) Product
sections.body: \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta=a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3\), a scalar. It is commutative and distributes over addition. Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=0\). The angle satisfies \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}\), the projection of \(\vec b\) along \(\vec a\) is \(\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|}\), and the work done by a force is \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S\).

sections.heading: Direction Cosines
sections.body: If \(\vec r\) makes angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) with the positive \(x,y,z\)-axes then \(l=\cos\alpha=\dfrac{x}{|\vec r|}\), \(m=\cos\beta=\dfrac{y}{|\vec r|}\), \(n=\cos\gamma=\dfrac{z}{|\vec r|}\). They satisfy \(l^2+m^2+n^2=1\), and \((l,m,n)\) are the components of the unit vector \(\hat r\).

sections.heading: The Cross (Vector) Product
sections.body: \(\vec a\times\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\,\hat n\), a vector perpendicular to both \(\vec a\) and \(\vec b\) whose direction follows the right-hand rule. It is anti-commutative: \(\vec b\times\vec a=-\vec a\times\vec b\). In components it is the determinant with rows \(\hat i\ \hat j\ \hat k\); \(a_1\ a_2\ a_3\); \(b_1\ b_2\ b_3\). Vectors are parallel exactly when \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\).

sections.heading: Area and Moment
sections.body: The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides \(\vec a,\vec b\) is \(|\vec a\times\vec b|\) and the area of the triangle is \(\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|\). A unit vector perpendicular to both is \(\pm\dfrac{\vec a\times\vec b}{|\vec a\times\vec b|}\). The moment (torque) of a force \(\vec F\) acting at a point with position vector \(\vec r\) about the origin is \(\vec M=\vec r\times\vec F\).

sections.heading: Scalar Triple Product
sections.body: \([\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)\) is a scalar equal to the \(3\times3\) determinant of the components. A cyclic change leaves it unchanged, \([\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=[\vec b\ \vec c\ \vec a]=[\vec c\ \vec a\ \vec b]\), and a swap of two vectors reverses its sign. Also \(\vec a\cdot\vec b\times\vec c=\vec a\times\vec b\cdot\vec c\): the dot and the cross can be interchanged.

sections.heading: Volume and Coplanarity
sections.body: The volume of the parallelepiped with edges \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c\) is \(|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|\); the volume of the tetrahedron is \(\tfrac16|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|\). Three vectors are coplanar exactly when \([\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=0\). Four points \(A,B,C,D\) are coplanar when \([\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}]=0\).

definitions.definition: A quantity with both magnitude and direction.
The vector \(\overrightarrow{OP}\) from the origin to the point \(P\).
A vector of magnitude \(1\); \(\hat r=\vec r/|\vec r|\).
One of the eight regions of space cut by the three coordinate planes.
\(\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta\), a scalar.
Two non-zero vectors with \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=0\).
\(l,m,n\), the cosines of the angles a vector makes with the axes; \(l^2+m^2+n^2=1\).
\(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S\), the dot product of force and displacement.
\(\vec a\times\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\,\hat n\), a vector perpendicular to both.
Curl the fingers from \(\vec a\) to \(\vec b\); the thumb points along \(\vec a\times\vec b\).
\([\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)\).
Vectors lying in one plane; \([\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]=0\).
A solid with three pairs of parallel faces; its volume is \(|[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]|\).

examTips: In the section formula \(AP:PB=m:n\), the point nearer to \(A\) carries the larger weight of \(\vec b\): \(\vec r=\dfrac{n\vec a+m\vec b}{m+n}\).
The dot product is a scalar and the cross product is a vector; never write a scalar dotted or crossed with a vector.
For \(\vec a\times\vec b\) keep the minus sign on the \(\hat j\) term when expanding the determinant.
Perpendicular means \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=0\); parallel means \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\) (equal ratios of components).
A swap of two vectors in a triple product changes the sign; a cyclic change does not.
Volume of a tetrahedron is one sixth of the triple product; area of a triangle is half the cross product.
